rounds.name: HR Interview

questions.text: Family background, upbringing, places visited.
Which project taught the most valuable life lessons and which one presented the biggest challenges?
Questions about DE&I framework and how you align with it.
Encountered any unethical practices and how you reacted.
Any questions you have for the interviewer about company expectations on beliefs and values.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.description: 40‑minute interview covering projects, case studies, and technical depth.

questions.text: Discussion of ‘Smart Returns’ project: problem statement, solution, workflow, technology integration.
Case study on demand‑based shipping feature for Amazon; demand forecasting models.
Estimated accuracy of ML model for demand forecasting.
Handling the 20% inaccuracy in demand forecasting.

tips.text: Placements are one of the most trying yet important phases of life and you will definitely come out on the other side, a stronger and more confident person.
ATS score checker : http://resumeworded.com/ (try to get >80)

Python essentials : Neetcode YT playlist , Blind 75 , Python for Everybody by University of Michigan (Coursera certification). Keep revising CS fundamentals (OS, CCN, DBMS, OOPs) as they are asked in a lot of tests and interviews both.

Aptitude : IndiaBix Start aptitude practice early on! Do not underestimate it or think “yeh toh easy hai ho hi jayega”. Speed and accuracy only comes through consistent practice and you can’t go from 0-100 in aptitude just in one night before your test.
For GDs, build your communication skills and quick thinking as they look for people who add value to the discussion by stating relevant points in a concise and articulate manner.

On your interview day, remain calm and composed and meditate/listen to songs/think of God (whatever works for you). Try to focus more on the process rather than the outcome to stop overthinking and believe in yourself!!!
Luck is a huge factor in every step of the process, so don’t take failures personally and just keep trying and improving yourself every day.

rounds.name: Aptitude Round
rounds.description: The Aptitude Round consisted of 100 questions covering Quantitative Aptitude, Geometry, Verbal Ability, and Logical Reasoning to be solved in 1 hour. The quantitative section included problems on percentages, ratios, time and work, and geometry-based questions. The verbal section tested grammar, reading comprehension, and vocabulary, while the reasoning section focused on analytical thinking. In addition to these, there were a few behavioral and situational questions. Overall, the round focused on both technical and behavorial assessment. This round followed a +4 -1 marking scheme.

questions.text: If your team member isn’t contributing effectively, what would you do?

rounds.name: Coding Round
rounds.description: Round 2 consisted of two sections – the first focused on basic Python MCQs, while the second included easy-level coding questions similar to those found on LeetCode. The only programming language allowed was Python.

rounds.name: Group Discussion Round
rounds.description: The topic given to us was “Technology: Boon or Bane.” Candidates who expressed their points in a clear, concise, and professional manner, speaking confidently and with good articulation, were the ones selected for the next round.

questions.text: Technology: Boon or Bane

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.description: The interview was primarily focused on Python and Machine Learning. The interviewer was very particular about the answers and often went into detailed discussions. He began by asking me to introduce myself. Since I had researched Mahindra Finance beforehand, I knew that one of its key sectors deals with loan approval, which aligned well with my credit risk modelling project. I mentioned this connection during my introduction, which led him to ask several project-related questions. The discussion then shifted to model evaluation metrics, where he asked me to explain precision, recall, and accuracy, and to justify which metric mattered the most in my project context. After that, he presented a case study scenario. The interview concluded with me asking him three questions about Mahindra Finance’s advancements in Machine Learning and how the company is integrating AI into its operations. Overall, it was a highly engaging and technical discussion that tested both conceptual understanding and practical problem-solving.

questions.text: introduce myself
which algorithm I had used
explain SMOTE along with its advantages and disadvantages
draw and explain the working of Random Forest and justify why it performed better than XGBoost in my case
write the pandas query for merging them using the ID column as the key
detailed questions about the types of columns in my dataset and their relevance
explain precision, recall, and accuracy, and to justify which metric mattered the most in my project context
If Uber ride prices suddenly increase from ₹400 to ₹800 within 10 minutes in the same location, how would you identify and fix the bug in your ML model?
describe the parameters and features I would use in such a model
If all drivers in a certain area stop accepting Uber rides and instead take private trips, how would your model detect such behavior?
how I would determine peak hours without having an existing dataset
three questions about Mahindra Finance’s advancements in Machine Learning and how the company is integrating AI into its operations

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.description: The HR round surprisingly lasted for around 45 minutes, during which the HR was noting down my answers carefully. The discussion mainly revolved around situational and behavioral questions. I was given several case-based scenarios. The HR wanted to understand my thought process, decision-making, and ability to handle real-life workplace challenges. Overall, it was a situational round focused on assessing attitude, ethics, and teamwork rather than technical knowledge.

questions.text: how I would handle a situation where a team member is not contributing effectively
how I would respond if I witnessed something wrong happening around me

tips.text: during your 6th semester, shut out the noise around you and just believe in your hard work.
Study everything that’s commonly asked in interviews.
In placements, being a jack of all trades often works better than excelling in just one domain.
Practicing DSA is important, of course, but relying only on it won’t help much—only 4–5 companies are heavily DSA-focused and I realized it much much later.
The rest mostly have doable coding questions in their online assessments and give high importance to aptitude, which most students tend to ignore.
For interviews, know your resume inside out—every project, every line.
SQL is the underdog in placements, so make sure to practice it thoroughly beforehand.
When it comes to projects, having a simple project that you understand deeply is far better than having an overly complex one that you can’t explain properly.
Lastly, know your OS, CN, and DBMS concepts really well—many companies ask questions from these subjects.
End-moment preparation won’t help much here, so start early.
